strategy:
1. Approach and rationale
Use a restartable differential-evolution (DE) population search directly on the N samples of h. Seed the population with the validated supplied construction, then evolve feasible vectors using whole-vector mutation and crossover. Project each trial onto the joint box-and-sum feasible set, and use the exact evaluator score for all selection and final comparisons. Keep the supplied construction as a protected fallback.

This is materially different from the supplied SLSQP epigraph search and from the earlier projected-gradient continuation and pair-transfer/annealing search designs: it uses no gradient, epigraph solver, coordinate-pair move, or annealing acceptance. It recombines differences between several full candidate vectors and uses generational survival plus explicitly bounded diversity restarts.

The mathematical facts are that the evaluator uses finite, non-circular correlation over all 2N-1 lags, and that products of h entries make the objective nonconvex. DE and projection do not make that objective convex or establish a global optimum. The search heuristic is that population differences can explore correlated directions and diverse basins that local gradient or single-pair moves may not reach. Projection can distort a trial, and a finite population and generation budget can still miss better candidates. Do not claim an improvement or attainment of the target score; return only the best feasible candidate found by the executed program.

2. Mathematical specification
For runtime dimension N >= 1, set dx=2/N and m=N/2. The feasible set is K={h in R^N: 0<=h_i<=1 for every i, sum_i h_i=m}. For each integer lag s from -(N-1) through N-1, define the finite-overlap sum
q_s(h)=sum_{i=max(0,-s)}^{min(N-1,N-1-s)} h_i*(1-h_(i+s)).
The overlap at a nonzero lag is only the indices in these limits; do not wrap indices or fill missing boundary terms. The q_s values are the full linear correlation values, possibly in reverse lag order, so the authoritative objective is
C(h)=dx*max_s q_s(h)=max(np.correlate(h,1-h,mode='full'))*(2.0/N).
Minimize C over K. Do not replace this expression with an autocorrelation identity or a circular correlation.

The DE population has P feasible vectors x_i in R^N with exact-score fitness C(x_i). For target i, choose mutually distinct indices r1,r2,r3, all different from i, and form the mutant
v_i=x_r1+F_DE*(x_r2-x_r3),
where the default mutation scale is F_DE=0.7. Since every population vector sums to m, this mutant also sums to m before crossover. Form a binomial-crossover vector u_i coordinatewise: use v_i[j] when a fresh uniform draw is less than CR or j equals a separately drawn forced coordinate j_rand; otherwise use x_i[j]. Crossover can break the sum constraint and either operation can violate box bounds, so set the actual trial to the joint projection P_K(u_i), not to a clipped or rescaled vector.

The joint Euclidean projection has coordinates P_K(z)_j=clip(z_j-lambda,0,1), with lambda chosen so that sum_j clip(z_j-lambda,0,1)=m. The sum is continuous and nonincreasing in lambda. Bracket a root with low=min(z)-1 and high=max(z), then use bisection. Correct the small residual sum error by moving coordinates only into available box slack. If the projected trial is feasible and its exact score is lower than the target score by the specified tolerance, replace that target. This is a derivative-free heuristic for a nonconvex objective, not a supported convex-solver formulation or a global-optimality claim.

3. Implementation procedure
1. Write one complete program with run(seed=42, **kwargs) at top level. Put helper functions at top level; do not use closures or lambdas. Use float64 NumPy arrays and a single seeded NumPy Generator; NumPy alone is sufficient. Do not use filesystem or network access, parallel execution, or printed progress. Do not redefine evaluate_erdos_solution or initial_h_values, and do not embed or reconstruct parent entries. Compute the score inside the program using the exact evaluator formula.

2. Resolve the seed, parent, and dimension inside run. Try np.random.default_rng(seed); if seed initialization raises an exception, use np.random.default_rng(42). Read the optional parent with globals().get('initial_h_values') and attempt conversion to a float64 array. A finite, one-dimensional, nonempty parent is usable and determines N from its full length; do not truncate, resample, or change resolution. Use the parent vector directly as the baseline if it satisfies the box and sum checks. Otherwise project the finite parent with the joint projector. If projection or validation fails, use the uniform feasible vector of length N, while retaining that parent-derived N.

Treat a malformed, empty, or nonfinite parent as unavailable. Without a usable parent, accept kwargs.get('n_points',70) only if it is an integer or NumPy integer, is not a Boolean, and lies in [1,999]; otherwise use N=70. Set the no-parent baseline to h_i=0.5. Set m=N/2 in either case. For N=1, return a feasible baseline after exact scoring without DE. For a parent with N>999, retain its feasible baseline and exact-score it, but skip the population search. Do not change N to seek a lower score at another resolution.

3. Implement top-level is_feasible(h,N,m) and project_box_sum(z,N,m) helpers. is_feasible requires shape (N,), finite entries, bounds within 1e-12 of [0,1], and abs(sum(h)-m)<=1e-10*max(1,N). The projector first checks the input shape and finiteness; if invalid, or if its magnitude is so extreme that safe bracketing is unavailable, return the uniform vector. Otherwise use low=min(z)-1 and high=max(z), perform 80 bisection iterations using mid=low+(high-low)/2, and move low upward when sum(clip(z-mid,0,1))>m, otherwise move high downward. Form the clipped vector at the final midpoint.

Correct residual r=m-sum(h) deterministically in index order. If r>0, add at most 1-h_i to each coordinate; if r<0, subtract at most h_i. Recompute the residual and repeat a correction pass if needed. Clamp only rounding overshoots caused by an individual update, then recompute and correct the sum again. Return the result only after bounds, finiteness, and the stated sum tolerance pass; otherwise return the uniform vector. Never use clipping followed by rescaling. The uniform vector is feasible for every N>=1.

4. Implement a top-level exact_score(h,N) helper. Reject a wrong shape or nonfinite input with positive infinity. Otherwise calculate corr=np.correlate(h,1.0-h,mode='full'), check that it is finite, and return float(np.max(corr)*(2.0/N)); return positive infinity if correlation or score is nonfinite or the operation fails. All candidates must also pass is_feasible before their score is used for selection. This helper evaluates every finite lag in the required linear-correlation convention.

5. Build the initial population with a top-level helper taking the baseline, N, m, P, and the RNG. Put an unchanged copy of the feasible baseline in the population first. Then propose, in this order, the complement 1-baseline, a seeded permutation of baseline, projected baseline-plus-Gaussian perturbations with standard deviations 0.02, 0.06, 0.15, and 0.30, a projected uniform random vector on [0,1], a projected Bernoulli vector with entries 0 or 1, and two projected Fourier profiles. For each Fourier profile use i=0,...,N-1, R=min(6,floor((N-1)/2)), and z_i=0.5+A*sum_{r=1}^R[(a_r*cos(2*pi*r*i/N)+b_r*sin(2*pi*r*i/N))/r], with independent standard-normal a_r,b_r and amplitudes A=0.12 and A=0.24. If R=0, the profile is just 0.5.

Project every proposal that is not already known feasible. Retain candidates in construction order, discarding a duplicate when its infinity-norm distance from a retained candidate is at most 1e-10. If fewer than P candidates have been obtained, make at most 20*P further attempts, alternating projected baseline-plus-noise proposals with noise standard deviation drawn log-uniformly from [0.03,0.35] and projected uniform random proposals. If the cap is still not reached, fill remaining slots with copies of feasible population members; duplicate population vectors are permitted. Validate every stored vector. This procedure uses the parent directly when feasible and still gives a diverse population when the baseline is uniform.

6. Implement a top-level DE search helper. Score the initial population with exact_score, initialize the global best to the baseline and its score, and update it only when a feasible finite candidate improves the score by more than 1e-12. For each generation, copy the population and scores to an immutable generation snapshot and initialize the next generation as those copies. For each target i, sample r1,r2,r3 without replacement from population indices other than i. Form v_i using the formula in section 2. Generate an independent length-N crossover mask with probability CR=0.85 per coordinate and force one uniformly drawn coordinate j_rand to come from v_i. Construct u_i from the mutant and snapshot target according to that mask, reject it if nonfinite, project it with project_box_sum, and validate it.

Calculate the exact score of each feasible trial. Replace snapshot target i in the next population only if trial_score < snapshot_score_i-1e-12; otherwise keep the target. Update the global best from every accepted trial that beats the global score by more than 1e-12. Use only the snapshot as the donor pool for a generation, so updates are synchronous and the result does not depend on target traversal order. Never accept a candidate on the basis of a surrogate score.

7. Add bounded stagnation restarts to the DE helper. Record the global-best score at the start of each generation. If the generation ends without a decrease greater than 1e-12, increment a stagnation counter; otherwise reset it to zero. When the counter reaches the tier-specific limit in section 4 and restart quota remains, construct a fresh population containing the global best and the best-scoring current population members up to one quarter of P, with at least two members when possible. Fill three quarters of remaining slots with project_box_sum(best_h+sigma*normal,m), and one quarter with project_box_sum(rng.uniform(0,1,N),m), rounding the counts so the final population has exactly P members. Use sigma=0.14 for the first restart and sigma=0.05 for the second. Score and validate every new member, reset stagnation, and increment the restart count. If restart quota is exhausted and stagnation reaches twice the tier-specific limit, stop early. All restart decisions and random draws run inside the generated program. Preserve the global best throughout and return it if a generation or restart encounters an exception.

8. In run, score the baseline before searching and keep it as an explicit fallback. Select the tier from N as specified in section 4, build the population, and call the DE helper only when search is enabled. Wrap population construction and search in failure handling: on an unusable proposal, nonfinite score, or exception, reject the affected proposal or stop that search branch without losing the best valid candidate already available. A failure of the whole search returns the baseline. Do not use the target value 0.3808 as an acceptance rule; selection is by exact score only.

9. Before returning, independently project the search result and baseline, validate both, and recompute both exact scores. Choose the search result only if it is feasible, has a finite score, and beats the baseline by more than 1e-12; otherwise retain the baseline. If projection or validation of the selected result fails, use the feasible baseline, or the uniform vector if the baseline is invalid, and recompute the score. Return a one-dimensional float64 h_values, a Python float c5_bound, and int(N), in that order.

4. Search choices and useful variations
Use these defaults without preliminary measurements. For 1<=N<=1, skip search. For 2<=N<=96 use P=48, at most 120 generations, a stagnation limit of 24 generations, and at most two restarts. For 97<=N<=192 use P=32, at most 80 generations, a stagnation limit of 20, and at most one restart. For 193<=N<=384 use P=20, at most 40 generations, a stagnation limit of 16, and at most one restart. For 385<=N<=999 use P=12, at most 20 generations, a stagnation limit of 10, and no restarts. For a parent with N>999, skip search. The supplied 70-sample parent uses the first search tier. The population size is always at least four when DE runs.

Use F_DE=0.7, CR=0.85, the 1e-12 score-improvement tolerance, the initialization and restart amplitudes in section 3, and 80 projection bisection iterations. The generation cap includes generations used before and after restarts. Meaningful bounded variations are P=32-64 and 80-160 generations for N<=96; F_DE=0.55-0.85; CR=0.70-0.95; and no more than two small-N restarts. A coder may retain the defaults without experiments. Correctness requirements do not vary: keep the parent resolution, use the exact full finite correlation for score comparisons, enforce box and sum jointly, retain the baseline fallback, and return the best exact-score feasible candidate. Do not claim a target score in advance.

5. Numerical robustness and memory use
Use float64 for parents, population vectors, projections, and scores. Reject nonfinite raw DE trials before projection. The projector must handle invalid or extreme proposals by returning a feasible uniform vector and must verify its own residual correction. A projected fallback may become a duplicate population member; this is safe, although it can reduce diversity. Check every initialization, restart, and trial for finite values and feasibility before scoring or storing it. If a correlation or score is nonfinite, reject that candidate. Catch local exceptions and preserve the best valid candidate and protected baseline.

Each score uses one np.correlate result of length 2N-1 and requires O(N^2) direct work; projection and mutation require O(N) work. The search uses O(PN) population memory plus O(N) temporary vectors and correlation storage. Do not construct a dense lag-by-coordinate Jacobian, Hessian, or N-by-N table. The tiered population and generation limits bound single-CPU work, and searches above 999 parent samples are disabled. If no trial improves the baseline, return the baseline. If there is no usable parent and search fails, return the uniform feasible vector. DE is heuristic and provides no global-optimality guarantee.

6. Runtime safeguards and return contract
The generated program itself must check the optional parent conversion, dimensionality, length, and finite values; use its full length when usable; and otherwise validate kwargs.get('n_points',70) and apply the specified fallback. It must implement candidate feasibility checks for shape (N,), finite values, bounds, and sum. Every population member, mutation trial, restart member, final candidate, and fallback must be feasible before it is scored or returned. Keep the baseline available regardless of population replacement.

Implement the score internally as max(np.correlate(h,1.0-h,mode='full'))*(2.0/N), including all 2N-1 linear lags. Use this exact score for initialization, greedy selection, best-candidate storage, final comparison, and the returned c5_bound. On any search failure, choose the best valid candidate already stored or the baseline. On any failed final validation, use the feasible baseline, or h_i=0.5 if no usable parent existed, and recompute its exact score. Return exactly (h_values, c5_bound, n_points); produce no other output and do not claim that the program has reached the requested target.
